Tap Behaviors

Tap Behaviors provide deterministic, ordered observation points within the Processing Layer of the pipeline. Tap behaviors allow engineers to execute side effects against immutable pipeline values without influencing derivation, reduction, control flow, or state commitment.

Tap Contract Summary

  • Tap functions may perform side effects
  • Tap functions must not mutate pipeline values
  • Tap functions must not return values
  • Tap functions do not influence pipeline control flow
  • Errors thrown during tap execution propagate as Vault errors

The Tap contract guarantees that tap execution remains observational and isolated. Tap behaviors do not derive values, do not mutate state, and do not emit snapshots. Their sole responsibility is to observe the pipeline value at a precise execution boundary and react externally.

Tap execution is deterministic and ordered. Multiple tap functions execute sequentially in the exact order they are registered during FeatureCell initialization.

Tap Stage

The Tap stage exists within the Processing Layer and provides two distinct execution boundaries: Before Tap and After Tap.

  • Before Tap executes after filtering and before reducer execution.
  • After Tap executes immediately after reducer execution.

Both tap stages receive the immutable upstream pipeline value. Tap functions are invoked strictly for observation and side-effect execution. They must treat the pipeline value as read-only.

If a tap function throws an error, the error is promoted to a Vault error and the current pipeline execution is terminated. No snapshot is emitted for that execution.

Core Pipeline Stage

The Tap stage is a core pipeline stage and is always present as part of the FeatureCell lifecycle. The core tap behaviors coordinate execution of engineer-supplied tap callback functions. Tap behaviors do not mutate values, resume execution, or alter pipeline outcomes.

Available Tap Behaviors

The Tap stage is a core pipeline stage and is always present. Engineers supply tap callback functions that are executed by the core tap behaviors at the appropriate execution boundary.

Core Tap Behaviors
FeatureCell Initialization

Tap behaviors expose fluent configuration APIs that allow engineers to register tap callback functions during FeatureCell initialization.

These APIs do not execute tap functions directly. They record ordered callback lists that are invoked later by the Tap stage during pipeline execution.
